cis_text.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit

ai_guidance.llm: Encrypt sensitive model-related data, including datasets, embeddings, outputs, and intermediate representations, while in transit to protect confidentiality and integrity during network transfer.
ai_guidance.agent: Encrypt all agent tool communication channels and agent-to-agent messaging in transit using approved cryptographic standards.
ai_guidance.mcp:
Require TLS 1.2 or later for Streamable HTTP. Validate certificates and reject weak ciphers and downgrade attempts. For stdio, protect data via OS process isolation, least-privilege execution, and endpoint encryption; treat any subsequent network calls from the server to backend APIs as in-transit data requiring TLS. Ensure back-end API calls from servers also use TLS.

Gateways must terminate TLS with proper certificate management and can use mutual TLS for higher security. For high-risk deployments, use mutual
TLS between gateway and server and enforce strict certificate validation.

evidence.rationale: Encryption in transit directly mitigates readable interception of network traffic.
Transport encryption directly constrains interception and manipulation of communications.

limits: A claim shows that a control can mitigate a technique. It does not show that an implementation is effective.
'none' or 'no_row' means the mapping has no mitigating control. It does not mean that no defence exists.
Claims use ATT&CK Enterprise 16.1, the version that the source mapping uses. See later_version for changes in newer versions.
CIS claims (cis_claims and cis/safeguards) use ATT&CK Enterprise 19.1, the version that the CIS mapping uses.

ATLAS data is version 5.6.0, the legacy ATLAS file. It is not the current ATLAS release (v2026.10 on 2026-11-08). An empty mitigation list means that ATLAS 5.6.0 links no mitigation, not that no mitigation exists. agent_related is derived by this project from names.
